decision: Public signup and household onboarding; retained household 1 remains excluded

aws_runtime_acceptance.operator_settings: Updated locally to match the observed live release and public-registration policy

browser.environment: Local Chromium; mocked Cognito SDK; no live identity or email

limits: Test groups overlap; counts are not a unique-test total.
Initial DB tests skipped while local MySQL was stopped; rerun against a new isolated local MySQL 8.4 succeeded.
Website and ECS are confirmed on release 16f87ea; publication is distinct from end-to-end acceptance.
Public signup, email confirmation, password reset, and test-account TOTP enrollment/sign-in challenge passed for synthetic Cognito users.
The synthetic household owner/member flow passed; a nonmember request for retained household 1 returned 404 without data.
No live OCR document was submitted during this acceptance run.

Current-release PITR and snapshot restores, API task replacement, RDS and Redis failovers, and API rollback were performed and verified; recovery evidence is recorded outside the repository and the 99-gate preflight is GO.

An initial restore probe used a stale bootstrap image and returned 404 for the current readiness route; it was excluded, its resources were cleaned, and both restores passed when repeated with API release :38.
The API rollback temporarily used :37, which disables public registration; :38 was restored and verified healthy afterward.

Two synthetic Cognito users were created and confirmed, then deleted; their DB profiles/history and one synthetic household were cleaned. Four one-off bootstrap tasks were started and stopped: one by its environment guard, then read-only inspection, cleanup, and cleanup verification.
No pre-existing user, household, production schedule, or provider key was changed.
